statement: Several Austin taprooms and brewpubs appear in the market-map sample with an integrated kitchen (Pinthouse, Lazarus, Brewtorium listed); the sample is small.
what_must_be_true: Integrated kitchens are table stakes, so NASHA's kitchen must be judged on its own merit.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv rows 2-9: Yelp listings (T2) and T1 summaries; pages not opened.
limitation: Yelp sample is small and not representative; menus not examined.
cheapest_test: Founder lists every brewery kitchen on site visits and phone calls.

statement: Craft-beer drinkers in Austin choose by style and brand, with IPA-led lists common.
what_must_be_true: A lager and wheat-led list must find enough drinkers who want it, not just be different.
existing_evidence: Repo notes a hazy-IPA focus at one brewpub (T1/T2); no consumer data on style preference.
limitation: One venue only; production share is not drinker preference.
cheapest_test: Compare current tap lists of several taprooms in a simple table.

statement: Austin guests will order a lager-first or wheat-first beer list when food is Indian-Mexican.
what_must_be_true: Guests find the style fit appealing and repeat-order it; brewer confirms the styles are distinguishable.
existing_evidence: None. No brewing or tasting has occurred.
limitation: Entirely untested; no customers, no beer.
cheapest_test: Structured tasting with bought-in beers matched to dishes, brewer present.

statement: Austin has accepted Indian food paired with beer: Whip In was reported as an Indian-immigrant-family pub and brewery.
what_must_be_true: The precedent reflects durable demand, not only one family's local loyalty.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv row 17: T1 search summaries; current brewing status unknown.
limitation: Pages not opened; ownership changed in 2017 per summaries; reasons unknown.
cheapest_test: Founder visits or calls to learn current status and menu.

statement: Indian-Mexican fusion businesses are reported in Austin (T1 summaries, pages not opened): Nasha (reported), Sivestar, Kurry Takos, Taco Twist, Austin Taco Project, Urban Turban (Round Rock).
what_must_be_true: NASHA must not claim to be first or only; whether any of these trades today, or has an audience, is unknown.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv rows 16-21 and COMPETITIVE-DIFFERENTIATION.md; T1, status unconfirmed.
limitation: Search summaries only; current operation of most is UNKNOWN.
cheapest_test: Founder checks each operator's current status by phone or visit.

statement: Austin diners are open to fusion with a clear, named identity.
what_must_be_true: Openness extends to Indian-Mexican specifically and to a brewery setting.
existing_evidence: Yelp review volumes for several named fusion restaurants (T2) in market-map.csv rows 22-23.
limitation: Review counts are not demand for NASHA; no review text read; ratings are user aggregates.
cheapest_test: Short guest interviews on fusion appetite using plain menu cards.

statement: Some Austin guests would reject Indian-Mexican fusion as novelty or as disrespectful to either cuisine.
what_must_be_true: Cultural advisors and community interviews find the pairing framed with care is welcome.
existing_evidence: None. No cultural advisor review has occurred.
limitation: Reception unknown; advisors own this judgement.
cheapest_test: Cultural advisor review of concept and menu wording before any public use.

statement: Austin appears to have many Indian restaurants in the Yelp sample; whether they substitute for a NASHA meal is an inference, not an observation.
what_must_be_true: NASHA offers a reason to choose it over a familiar Indian dinner, such as beer pairing or group fit.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv rows 11-13: Yelp indpak listings (T2), many well reviewed.
limitation: Yelp sample only; menus, prices and beer attach unknown.
cheapest_test: Ask Indian-dining interviewees what they would trade off to visit a brewery.

statement: Indian diners in Austin want a beer-forward venue with Indian-influenced food.
what_must_be_true: Enough Indian-dining households see beer and food together as a reason to visit.
existing_evidence: None directly; Whip In is a historical precedent only.
limitation: No NASHA demand data; precedent may not generalise.
cheapest_test: Interview Indian-dining households about beer-with-dinner habits.

statement: Austin has deep supply of Mexican restaurants, and birria is already sold by specialists.
what_must_be_true: Goat birria that reads as goat is distinct and acceptable to guests (D-54: no beef or pork).
existing_evidence: market-map.csv rows 14-15: Yelp listings (T2); birria protein not established.
limitation: Protein, volume and goat availability unknown.
cheapest_test: Check menus of birria sellers; later a chef-cooked tasting.

statement: Mexican-dining guests will accept Indian spice logic in a taco or birria format.
what_must_be_true: Guests rate the result as coherent and tasty, and not as a gimmick.
existing_evidence: None. Nothing has been cooked or tasted.
limitation: Untested; chef owns the recipes.
cheapest_test: Blinded tasting of chef-cooked dishes with recruited guests.

statement: Experiential venues in Austin draw visits through activity and programming (arcade bar, music, social club).
what_must_be_true: A food-and-beer story, tours or events can be a reason to visit without an activity hook.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv rows 28-30: LOW and T1 or T2 sources.
limitation: Revenue and food attach unknown; reasons for visits not shown.
cheapest_test: Offer a small tasting-night pop-up and record who attends and why.

statement: A designed brewhouse-as-centrepiece hall drives repeat visits in Austin.
what_must_be_true: Guests return for the room and a lender accepts the capital need in a consolidating market.
existing_evidence: None. Central Machine Works is one reported converted-shed example (T1).
limitation: Design alone may not drive repeats; cost unknown; architect not consulted.
cheapest_test: Architect and cost review; tour-style pop-up.

statement: Patios appear as a common feature in the sampled Austin taproom and beer-garden listings and press snippets.
what_must_be_true: Shade is baseline, so only demonstrably better cooling or comfort could be a hook.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv rows 31-32: Yelp listings (T2) and press snippets.
limitation: Actual shade or cooling features at competitors unknown.
cheapest_test: Visit several patios at different times and note shade and comfort.

statement: Guests will choose a venue because of a climate-engineered patio.
what_must_be_true: Heat discomfort is a real barrier and guests value relief enough to switch venues.
existing_evidence: None. No guest data; competitors may already shade.
limitation: No willingness data; architect input needed.
cheapest_test: Short interviews plus counts of patio use at several venues across seasons.

statement: Segment: groups with mixed diets and mixed ages (including vegetarian guests) are underserved by one-cuisine taprooms.
what_must_be_true: Groups report splitting plans because of menu limits and would pick a mixed-diet menu.
existing_evidence: None. A weak signal from one late-night vegetarian truck listing (T2).
limitation: No group-ordering data; paneer-in-tortilla already sold locally.
cheapest_test: Group-ordering pop-up or interviews with organisers.

statement: Segment: Indian and Mexican communities in Austin are core guests, not just curiosity seekers.
what_must_be_true: Members of both communities say they would visit and recommend the venue.
existing_evidence: None.
limitation: No community interviews; size and attitudes UNKNOWN.
cheapest_test: Interview members of each community; cultural advisors guide approach.

statement: Segment: neighbourhood regulars rather than destination visitors will drive repeat sales.
what_must_be_true: A location exists where repeat local visits are plausible within the site budget.
existing_evidence: None. No site chosen.
limitation: Location, rent and trading area unknown.
cheapest_test: Document visit frequency in interviews; no site decision before this.

statement: The closest competitors for the visit are neighbourhood taco-and-beer places and fusion dinner restaurants, not Indo-Mex breweries.
what_must_be_true: Guests compare NASHA with those options at decision time.
existing_evidence: market-map.csv row 8 (Lazarus) and COMPETITIVE-DIFFERENTIATION.md; T1/T2.
limitation: Agent judgement from listings; guest behaviour not observed.
cheapest_test: Ask interviewees where they would go instead.

statement: No in-house brewery with an Indian-Mexican kitchen was found in a capped search; this does not prove none exists.
what_must_be_true: A site-based survey confirms the combination is unoccupied, or competitors are understood.
existing_evidence: AUSTIN-MARKET-MAP.md H1: Yelp sample and capped web searches (T1/T2).
limitation: Absence of results is not proof; search limits stated in the market map.
cheapest_test: Repeat search in person and by phone and list every brewery kitchen.

statement: Austin brewery market is consolidating, so capital discipline matters more than novelty.
what_must_be_true: Closures reflect market conditions that would also constrain a new entrant.
existing_evidence: AUSTIN-MARKET-MAP.md summary citing the landscape file; underlying source not reopened here.
limitation: Causes of closures unknown; figures not restated here.
cheapest_test: Read the landscape source and a trade-body report; ask an accountant.

statement: A reported same-name Austin restaurant (Nasha) may affect whether NASHA can operate under that name.
what_must_be_true: A trademark attorney clears or advises on the name; NASHA claims no rights.
existing_evidence: NASHA-CONFLICT-FACTS.md: T1 search summaries; no registry searched.
limitation: No legal conclusion; status and rights UNKNOWN.
cheapest_test: Send the conflict facts file to a trademark attorney.

statement: Austin is a good NASHA market only if guests, advisors and economics all validate together.
what_must_be_true: Guests choose NASHA over substitutes, communities respond well, the name is available, and unit economics hold.
existing_evidence: None. Every condition is UNTESTED.
limitation: Demand is an assumption until real customers validate it.
cheapest_test: Run the A and B tests in this file first; stop if two or more fail.

statement: Legal and regulatory constraints on a brewery with a kitchen and a pop-up route are resolved for Texas.
what_must_be_true: A Texas alcohol attorney and county health confirm a viable licensing path.
existing_evidence: None. Market map notes licensing is unresolved.
limitation: Professionals own this decision.
cheapest_test: Questions to a Texas alcohol attorney and county health.
